scope: Hash-bound AC1015/AC1021/AC1024 PERSUBENTMGR D63 peer traces and class-body/handle boundary observations

oda.document: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
oda.section: §20.1 common object framing; no PERSUBENTMGR-specific field schema

peerSchema.note: The PERSUBENTMGR class is marked unstable; dwg2.spec describes the layout as varying and its tail decode overruns or yields invalid cursor positions for these records. This trace is boundary evidence, not accepted semantic schema.

trace.failure: Peer then attempts subentity reads beyond the 24-byte object; decoded tail values are invalid and excluded.
The bounded peer decode stops after the eight candidate prefix values at the modern string/footer and handle boundary.
Candidate trailing count exceeds the remaining object bounds; the peer rejects the implied subentity vector as invalid.

whatThisSupports: The three hash-bound records share the eight-value candidate prefix also present in their paired DXF group-90 sequences.
Their object-data and handle-stream limits differ by version and bound the PERSUBENTMGR records.
The peer's proposed trailing count/subentity interpretation is not supported: it overruns AC1015, stops at the boundary for AC1021, and is out-of-bounds for AC1024.
whatThisDoesNotSupport: No exact per-field physical bit span is accepted from the unstable peer output; its step-vector cursor labels overflow and are not reliable.
No class-specific PERSUBENTMGR grammar, field semantics, producer-wide behavior, DXF output eligibility, or support claim is established.
conclusion.next: Find an independently maintained implementation or a native producer/consumer observation that distinguishes the class-specific body schema; keep unresolved records raw-carried or Partial and make no production interpretation change until then.
